---
title: "Build-pin drift attestation -- arm-recipe transient-window hardening re-seal (2026-11-11)"
---

Attestation record of the `arm-recipe-degraded-requeue` lane (one commit on
`main@2846dec`). Both live six-arm image builds of the generation-4
pre-ignition batch died in the same systematic class -- not in the recipe's
dependency logic, but in its transient-window retry budgets. This record
attests the remedy, the re-seal of the two affected blob pins, and the gates
that now hold the amended bytes. It is the second build-pin drift attestation:
the first (`vignettes/articles/devlog-2026-11-04-m7-build-pin-drift-attestation.qmd`)
re-anchored the pin ceremony to git blobs; this one amends a pinned file's
bytes under that ceremony.

Every hex below was emitted by command this session (git plumbing, `shasum
-a 256`, build-log files); no digest was typed from memory into any tool
call. The reading test (`bench/m7/tests/test_recipe_blob_pins.py`, group
(AM)) re-measures every pin claim here against git and disk on every suite
run -- this file is the narrative, the gate is the authority.

## 1. The failures, measured

Two sequential six-arm builds (`tools/p6_build_arms.py`, sigminer tree
recipe) each died at the CONSISTENCY stage, with different victims but one
shape:

- Run 1 (`/tmp/p6lane/logs/arms.build.log`):
  `FATAL:consistency: floater dplyr introduced unknown dependency lazyeval,dbi — refusing to install blind`
  (2851.5 s).
- Run 2 (`/tmp/p6lane/logs/arms.build2.log`):
  `CONSIST glue 1.3.2 breaks (glue >= 1.6.1) from stringr` → Archive walk for
  stringr → `CONSIST float stringr 1.6.0 -> 0.6` → `CONSIST gtable 0.3.5
  breaks (gtable >= 0.3.6) from ggplot2` → Archive walk for ggplot2 →
  `CONSIST float ggplot2 4.0.3 -> 0.8` →
  `FATAL:consistency: floater ggplot2 introduced unknown dependency reshape,proto — refusing to install blind`
  (3187.9 s, log line 176).

Run 2 also contains the silent case the die could not see: `pkgconfig` 2.0.3
canon candidates failed (bioconductor URL flakes) and the Archive walk
settled 2.0.2 at 2550.3 s with no marker.

The class: canon (CRAN-current) fetch failures inside transient proxy
windows exhausted the retry budget; the resolver then fell through to an
Archive floor-settle (silently, or loudly as a floater); the floater's fresh
imports sat outside the settled graph and the fail-closed die fired. The
reference recipe (`Dockerfile.sigminer.tree` lineage) built clean twice on
the same network, so the trigger is the current transient-window density,
not a defect in the dependency graph itself -- hence recipe hardening, not a
third plain retry.

## 2. The remedy (committed)

`bench/m7/adapters/install_sigminer_arm.R` amended, committed as
`0e7a27a9565f7a8a08331420b84452db070ee652` ("fix: harden arm installer
against transient-window floor-settles", parent
`2846decb245f9055196bcbc2ae8ffe09f8d45433`, 2026-11-11T06:26:53+08:00):

1. `resolveNode` marks an Archive-settled result `degraded = TRUE` when its
   canon candidates saw transient failures; a clean canon success returns
   unmarked.
2. The BFS requeues a degraded settle exactly once per node (`MAX_DEFER`
   budget, `seen` key re-opened) so canon gets a second chance before the
   graph accepts a floor-settle.
3. `MAX_TRY` 3 → 5 (the burst backoff rides 2+4+6+8+8 = 28 s per URL shape;
   both logs' windows out-lived the old 3-burst budget).
4. The CONSIST floater path no longer dies fail-closed on fresh imports: the
   imports join the graph through a fresh-import adoption BFS (resolve,
   DEFER on transient, degraded requeue, adopt with their own dependency
   subtrees).
5. `MAX_CONSIST` 3 → 5 (run 2 consumed two float rounds and died on the
   third; the loud die is kept for genuinely divergent graphs).

## 4. Gates

- `test_recipe_blob_pins.py` EXIT:0 -- both seal sites validate (seal commit
  == lineage head == last touch; blob-at-seal == blob-at-HEAD == on-disk
  bytes).
- `test_p6_roster`, `test_registry`, `test_p6_floor_governance`,
  `test_hardware_pin` all EXIT:0 against the amended tree.
- `test_batch_bridge_arm` EXIT:0 via `python3 -m tests.test_batch_bridge_arm`
  from `bench/m7`. Invocation note (pre-existing, unrelated to this
  amendment): the direct-script form `python3 tests/test_batch_bridge_arm.py`
  raises `ImportError: cannot import name 'coex_fixtures' from 'tests'`
  because the `tests` package then resolves to `bench/g0/tests`; the module
  invocation resolves `bench/m7/tests`, which owns `coex_fixtures.py`. The
  failure reproduces with main's copy byte-for-byte; module invocation is the
  sanctioned form for the m7 gates.

## 5. Custody

- Branch `arm-recipe-degraded-requeue`; installer amendment committed first
  (`0e7a27a…`), Dockerfile re-seal + this devlog land as the lane's second
  commit; one phase-PR to main.
- The six arm images are NOT yet rebuilt from the amended recipe: the image
  digests in `competitors/p6_arms.py` still speak the pre-hardening builds
  and flip only after the rebuilt roster attests 8/8 (SS3 law, one change
  set carrying the build-log witnesses).
- Zero real-data bytes (COSMIC) touched; zero sigminer refs touched; the
  reference recipe lineage and its settled parity rows are unaffected --
  this lane hardens the resolver's transient-window behavior only.
